text:
maya: heads up — p99 on the /generate endpoint spiked when we shifted fallback weight to variant_v2, dashboard shows a big jump but p50/p95 look stable

omar: saw that, looks like the merge is pulling samples from both variants but the origin tag isn't surfacing in the console

sophie: are we sure it's not sampling rate differences? variant_v2 gets fewer samples so a couple slow requests could skew p99

maya: i pulled raw traces, there are matching request_ids for slow tails and they all hit fallback. i'm leaning toward attribution issue in the rollup pipeline

ryan: quick check — does the router tag requests with "route_origin" or just the endpoint name?

omar: router currently emits endpoint + model_variant as a single label `endpoint: /generate|variant: v2` but our ingestion rollup flattens labels and drops variant on high-card routes

sophie: that's the crux — dropping variant reduces provenance and causes percentiles to mix indistinguishably. UX then shows endpoint p99 jump with no explanation

maya: suggestion: add a low-cardinality `sample_origin` tag that can be turned on for rollouts (e.g., `origin=fallback_v2`) so dashboards can show per-origin p99 without exploding cardinality

ryan: agree but internal API debate: should router set `sample_origin` or should the serving runtime set it? router has routing semantics, runtime has latency truth.

omar: pros/cons: router-level tag is immediate and cheap but can be stale if runtime falls back differently. runtime-level tag is authoritative but we'd need to add it to the token that ingestion consumes (adds a write path).

sophie: also need to consider quota/weight changes — when weights shift quickly p99 can flip. We might want a smoothing window in the console annotations to avoid alarming alerts for short-lived rebalances

maya: operational request — can we add an annotation on the latency chart to show rollout weight changes and quota adjustments? even a tiny line with weight % would help correlate

ryan: we can annotate from the routing service events stream. quick patch: pull rollout events into metrics pipeline as `annotation` with timestamp. low-risk.

omar: for the longer fix, propose: runtime emits `sample_origin` (v1/v2/fallback) at request completion, ingestion preserves that tag at rollup unless cardinality threshold exceeded, and console shows a toggle "group by sample origin". If cardinality would explode, disable toggle with a tooltip explaining why

maya: that sounds good. sophie, can you prototype toggle UX? Not a design project — just a checkbox and small legend showing origins + counts

sophie: i'll mock in an afternoon. proposing small-change flow: UI toggle + backend flag `preserve_origin=true` for rollout windows

ryan: one more thing — telemetry: we should emit sample counts per origin to detect under-sampled origins. If origin sample_count < N we add a caution badge next to p99 saying "low sample count — percentile unstable"

omar: implementation notes for infra: ingestion needs a safe path to store `sample_origin` as a single low-card string. don't add full variant name unless customer opt-in. keep it simple: `origin=fallback_v2`, `origin=primary`, `origin=canary`

maya: action items: 1) sophie mock UI toggle (ETA EOD tomorrow) 2) ryan add chart annotation for rollout weight events (PR) 3) omar prototype runtime tag emission + ingestion preserve flag 4) maya add alert suppression for transient weight shifts

deploy-bot: scheduled job: created ticket PLAT-4821 to track runtime tag + ingestion change (assignee: omar)

maya: thanks — if folks agree i'll add design + infra tickets and we can ship a small telemetry-only rollout before turning on preservation for all routes

ryan: +1

sophie: +1

omar: +1

maya: closing loop — we should also update the docs on percentile attribution and include a short note in the rollout playbook about gradual weight moves to avoid dashboards flipping
